answer: Deposits are visible in relic, and tide reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 31% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 127 aliases, and each one needs its own funded falcon account. Scaling to 110 identities multiplies that fee by 813 with no matching gain in influence. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
